links.outcome: Non-physician rater comprehension of original vs AI patient-friendly radiology reports (5-point Likert)
links.effect: Mean comprehension rose from 2.71 ± 0.73 for original reports to 4.69 ± 0.48 for patient-friendly reports (p < 0.001).
links.quote: The average comprehension score for the original report was 2.71 ± 0.73, while the score for the patient-friendly reports significantly increased to 4.69 ± 0.48 (p < 0.001).

links.outcome: Rate of artificial hallucinations and potentially harmful translations in AI-generated reports
links.effect: 1.12% artificial hallucinations and 7.40% potentially harmful translations.
links.quote: There were 1.12% artificial hallucinations and 7.40% potentially harmful translations.

unlisted_practices: AI-generated summary and recommendation sections for radiology reports

screen.reason: The study evaluates an LLM's baseline ability to translate spine MRI reports into patient-friendly summaries and generate recommendations, measuring comprehension and hallucinations without testing a specific organizational safeguard or deployment intervention.
